knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The procedure requires clear exits and fire equipment, secured cords and site-approved barriers that keep the public out of wet or hazardous zones.

Pausing, keeping the zone closed and reassessing the barriers before restoring access is correct. Where the work cannot be completed safely, the zone stays controlled and the supervisor is told before access is restored. Keeping the zone open with a verbal warning, or moving barriers to suit passers-by, is not acceptable.

Working in short sections, diverting pedestrians, drying each area and restoring access only after inspection is the correct approach. The worked example uses exactly this sequence. Closing the whole building for the day, mopping the entire corridor at once, or leaving the wet floor unmarked does not control the hazard.

Leaving a wet area unmarked while the work continues is the unsafe alternative, because the procedure requires wet-floor controls and site-approved barriers that keep the public out of wet or hazardous zones. Securing cords and hoses against trips, keeping exits clear and using approved barriers are the safe practices.
Zone changes are recorded, and access is restored only after inspection. Escalation goes to the supervisor, not only to the client.

practicalCriteria: Maintains clear exits, controls slips and trips, protects customer property and adapts controls during work.
Uses the authorised work order and site instructions
Recognises and escalates hazards or scope limitations
Records objective evidence and correction where needed
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Record of procedure step 3: Keep exits and fire equipment clear throughout the job.
Record of procedure step 4: Secure cords and hoses against trips, and use site-approved barriers to keep the public out of wet or hazardous zones.
Record of procedure step 8: Restore access only after the work zone has been inspected, and record the facts.
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 1 is not done: Confirm the actual work scope, the hazards and who can authorise changes before setting up.
Stop work if procedure step 4 is not done: Secure cords and hoses against trips, and use site-approved barriers to keep the public out of wet or hazardous zones.
Stop work if procedure step 5 is not done: Avoid moving customer valuables, and make sure tools do not damage walls, floors or furniture.
